answer: The timing of AI adoption in certain sectors affects the urgency and effectiveness of federal legislative responses by creating a disparity between the pace of AI development and the legislative process. Some sectors lag in AI adoption, resulting in a lower immediate need for targeted legislation. However, as AI products begin to integrate into these sectors, existing regulatory frameworks may struggle to meet their needs. This can lead to delays in legislative responses, as evidenced by the proposal-enactment gap, which can take over a year—up to 664 days—before new measures are enacted. Such delays can pose substantial downstream risks, especially when urgent interventions are required, as governance often lags behind the rapid development of AI models. Consequently, legislation that addresses 'old' risks may not adequately cover 'new' risks that emerge as AI capabilities evolve.
